ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a distinct pale snout. It features a granular belly and lacks webbing on its fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes coonoorensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow or orange webbing between its toes, which is absent in most other similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes coonoorensis* inhabits the high-altitude shola forests and grasslands of the Nilgiri Hills in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Coonoor bush frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects among forest floor vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes coonoorensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in terrestrial nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes coonoorensis* is endemic to the Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu, India, typically found at high elevations ranging from 1,800 to 2,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Coonoor Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink" notes, typically heard calling from dense vegetation within its montane forest habitat.
